header:
Date: 2028-01-17
Time: 14:30 PST
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya T, Diego R, Lena P (Redwood) — Ravi P, Nora W, Samir K, Elise C (Archipelago Ventures)
summary: Discovery focused on multi-tier fallback strategy (hosted -> dedicated -> private fallbacks), realistic SLA targets and contractual carve-outs for planned maintenance, and technical validation needs (prefix cache priming, multi-region KV cache consistency). Customer wants clear economic tradeoffs and an ops playbook for graceful degradation.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private fallback policies
SLA targets and carve-outs (planned maintenance, force majeure)
Cache consistency and prefix/KV cache behavior on failover
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intros — I'm Maya from Redwood, Diego and Lena on the line from our solutions team.
[00:07] Ravi (Archipelago/CTO): Thanks, Maya. I'm Ravi, CTO, Nora leads platform, Samir is our SRE, and Elise is here to listen from legal.
[00:15] Maya: Great. Goal for today is to understand your availability needs and how you'd like Redwood to behave in partial failures, multi-region issues, and what SLA commitments you need in contract.
[00:29] Nora: High level — our stack is customer-facing chat agents for investment advisors. We have sub-second expectations for core workflow but can tolerate slight degrade for long-running generation jobs. Main ask is: if Redwood hosted region goes down, what's the path and economic impact to fall back to dedicated or to our private cluster?
[00:45] Diego (SE): Good question. There are a few axes: routing policy, model compatibility, and state like KV cache or prefix caching that can affect cold-start. For hosted to dedicated fallbacks we do model version mapping and try to route to a compatible variant — but there can be a warmup penalty.
[01:05] Samir (SRE): When you say warmup, quantify? Our p50 needs to stay under 200ms for simple prompts, p95 under 800ms ideally.
[01:14] Diego: Under typical conditions with hot KV cache, you can see similar p50s. But on cross-region fallback where prefix cache is empty, you could see an initial 10–30% latency bump for some flows, and token cost changes if batching behavior differs.
[01:30] Ravi: That's a big one. We can't absorb long tails for our advisor flows. We need to codify an SLO-backed fallback that only triggers for sustained degradation and has an automatic rollback.
[01:40] Lena: We usually recommend a staged fallback: 1) route to healthy hosted region in same geo, 2) if unavailable, route to dedicated pool (if customer has reserved) or a Redwood-compatible multi-region hosted pool, 3) as last resort, route to private deployment if provisioned and warmed. Each step should have thresholds and a cooldown window.
[01:58] Nora: How do you handle KV cache consistency? If a user context is cached in Redwood hosted and we route to Private, is the history lost?
[02:08] Diego: Two points: KV cache for LLM inference is ephemeral and tied to the serving runtime instance; we do prefix/KV caching on the serving tier but we don't ship customer KV across environments automatically. For strict session continuity we recommend session-synchronization in your app layer or a shared prefix store (customer-managed) synced across regions.
[02:29] Samir: So in a fallback event the conversation could lose context unless we implement sticky session fallback. That would mean at least some UX mitigation (like short context resends) — understood.
[02:39] Elise (Legal): From a contract perspective we need clarity on what counts as an outage for SLA credits. Planned maintenance windows, third-party cloud provider maintenance, and force majeure — we want carve-outs but also clear RTO/RPO numbers.
[02:51] Maya: Absolutely. We can provide an SLA matrix with RTO/RPO bands and the exact credit formulas. Typical hosted SLA we offer is 99.9% for API availability with specified measurement windows; Dedicated has higher SLO targets and Private is customer-managed but we provide operational support SLAs.
[03:07] Ravi: Example: if we need 99.95% for mission-critical endpoints, can Redwood meet that on Hosted or we should plan Dedicated?
[03:15] Lena: 99.95% on Hosted is tricky globally unless you lean on multi-region active-active and reserve more capacity; Dedicated can be contracted with higher uptime guarantees since it's capacity you reserve and isolate.
[03:25] Nora: Cost question — what's the delta in sustained monthly cost to keep a warm dedicated fallback pool sized for our peak qps?
[03:34] Diego: We'll run numbers after you share qps and token/time distributions. As a rule of thumb: a small dedicated warm standby could cost roughly 40–60% of your peak reserved capacity depending on GPU types and autoscaling policy. There are also burst options to reduce that by using cross-tenant spare capacity.
[03:49] Samir: On autoscaling and throttles: will traffic throttled during failover contribute to 429s for end users? We need a graceful degradation strategy to avoid a sudden avalanche of errors.
[03:59] Diego: Yes — Redwood supports circuit-breaker policies and per-route throttling. In a failover we can configure traffic-steering rules that drop lower-priority requests (batch jobs) first and keep critical routes. You can also use 503 with Retry-After vs 429 depending on desired behavior.
[04:17] Ravi: Can we test this? We want a simulated failover test — send traffic to hosted region, then flip routing and watch the effect on p95 and error rates.
[04:26] Maya: We can do a joint runbook test in the technical deep dive. Diego can provide a script and we can coordinate a 1–2 hour window.
[04:33] Lena: We'll also provide an example rollback policy using canary traffic for model rollouts so that if a fallback model variant underperforms, traffic automatically shifts back.
[04:41] Nora: Side question — encryption and KMS. For Private we need to bring our own KMS and have HSM-backed keys. Is that supported?
[04:49] Diego: Yes — Private supports customer-managed KMS and you can enable HSM integrations. Hosted supports envelope encryption and Redwood-managed KMS by default, with options to integrate customer KMS for enterprise contracts.
[05:00] Elise: Audit logs and retention — we need at least seven years of audit trail for certain transactions and immutable logs for compliance. Can Redwood provide that for Hosted?
[05:08] Maya: Hosted provides standard audit logs for API calls; for extended retention we have add-on packages that push logs to customer-owned S3 or a log-archive. We'll include the retention options in the docs we send.
[05:19] Samir: Back to fallback — what about model mismatch? If hosted uses a quantized variant and dedicated uses a different precision model, will outputs vary significantly for downstream scoring?
[05:29] Diego: There can be small distributional shifts. Redwood offers model profiles with expected perf/quality metrics across precision/quantization. For critical pipelines we recommend pinned model versions across environments or preflight evals to measure delta with your prompt set.
[05:43] Ravi: Could Redwood run a quick eval on our 100 prompts to estimate delta?
[05:48] Maya: Yes, we can — send a subset of prompts under NDA and Diego's team will run a batch comparison.
[05:54] Nora: For the actual contract — we want clear definitions for partial degradation credits: for example, if p95 latency exceeds target for more than 10% of a monthly window, is that a partial credit?
[06:06] Lena: We'll propose a graded credit table — different buckets for p50/p95 availability and a path for disputed incidents (post-mortem with logs). We also include maintenance windows where SLA doesn't apply.
[06:16] Elise: One more legal ask — we need data residency guarantees. Some EU customers require data to stay in EU. How granular is region pinning?
[06:24] Diego: You can pin model serving to a region, and for Hosted we support region pinning. For Private we can run in your VPC in the region you choose. We'll call out data residency options in the security pack.
[06:34] Samir: Operational responsibilities during a failover — who runs the rollback? Do we want Redwood to have automated policies or do we trigger manually?
[06:41] Maya: Both are possible. Many customers choose automated policy for standard failovers with human-in-the-loop for escalation. We'll provide templates for both manual and automated playbooks.
[06:51] Ravi: Ok this was helpful. Quick recap?
[06:55] Maya: Recap: Redwood will send SLA matrix and sample graded credit table; Diego will prepare failover test script and rollback/canary examples; Archipelago to provide qps and prompt set; schedule a technical deep dive to run the simulated failover next week.
[07:10] Nora: Sounds good.
[07:13] Elise: Thanks. We'll review the legal packet once you send it.
[07:16] Maya: Great, will follow up. Thanks everyone.

Notes on transcript quality: some acronyms transcribed oddly in places (K V cache -> "K V cash"), minor speaker overlaps marked as interruptions.
